explanation: OEIS A055487 (least m with φ(m) = n!), M. F. Hasler: 'Unless n!+1 is prime, a(n)=pq where p is the least prime > sqrt(n!) such that (p−1) | n! and q=n!/(p−1)+1 is prime.' The formal p uses Nat.sqrt(n!) < p, equivalent to p > √(n!) since n! is not a perfect square for n ≥ 2. The excluded n are those with n! + 1 prime (covering n ≤ 3), and the conclusion asserts p exists (is prime) and a(n) = p·q. Faithful.
